_note: TECHNIQUES DATABASE for the operator/co-pilot (suggesting + checking) and the Kali driver stack. Complements the CVE RAG (NVD/KEV/EPSS/Exploit-DB) with the HOW: each technique class mapped to the Kali TOOL(s) and/or new CODE that test it, how to run an extensive+organized test, and the ORACLE that confirms. Deploy to /opt/aegis-rag; query with technique_search.py. Authorized/contained testing only; non-destructive by default.

techniques.how_to_test: service+version scan, HTTP tech fingerprint, WAF detect; feed versions to CVE RAG
techniques.oracle: confirmed versions/tech recorded; drives known-vuln pass

techniques.how_to_test: wordlist brute of dirs/files incl backup/config extensions; recurse; note 200/403/redirect
techniques.oracle: reachable sensitive path (backup, .git, admin, config) returns content

techniques.how_to_test: passive+active subdomain enum; resolve; port/service scan the live ones
techniques.oracle: new in-scope hosts discovered

techniques.how_to_test: probe /.git/, /.svn/, backup.zip/.tar.gz/.sql, editor swap files
techniques.oracle: source/backup downloadable -> real code (also a finding)
techniques.real_world_basis: agents used exposed creds/source

techniques.how_to_test: sqlmap on params/JSON/headers/cookies; --level/--risk up; --batch; test auth'd + per role
techniques.oracle: boolean/error/time/union confirms; sqlmap dumps a controlled value; DB oracle

techniques.how_to_test: inject $ne/$gt/$where/[$regex] in JSON bodies + query params
techniques.oracle: auth bypass or data returned that differs from control

techniques.how_to_test: inject ;/|/`$()` with a benign marker (sleep, callback) into params reaching a shell
techniques.oracle: time-delay or callback fires (blind); or command output reflected

techniques.how_to_test: inject {{7*7}} ${7*7} #{7*7} <%=7*7%> into fields rendered by a template engine; escalate to RCE per engine
techniques.oracle: output shows 49 (evaluated) not the literal; RCE marker fires
techniques.real_world_basis: a file-reference layer + template engine -> RCE

techniques.how_to_test: submit XML with external entity to a loopback/callback or file:///etc/passwd
techniques.oracle: file content returned or callback fires

techniques.how_to_test: inject markup into names/notes/desc that flow into email HTML or PDF; render in a mail sink/browser
techniques.oracle: markup executes in rendered email/PDF (else clean if text-only)
techniques.real_world_basis: attacker-controlled fields in outputs

techniques.how_to_test: dalfox on params + stored fields; check reflection contexts; DOM sinks
techniques.oracle: payload executes in a real browser DOM (alert/marker), not just reflected text

techniques.how_to_test: point a server-side fetch (webhook, url param, settings host) at a collaborator callback or internal/metadata (169.254.169.254)
techniques.oracle: callback listener receives a hit (blind); or internal-only content reflected; grey-box: fetch not behind an SSRF allow-list
techniques.real_world_basis: SSRF via an artifact repository = egress path

techniques.how_to_test: as role B, request role A's object IDs across every resource; compare per-role
techniques.oracle: 200 returning another owner's data where it should be 403/404
techniques.real_world_basis: cross-tenant token/object reuse

techniques.how_to_test: every role x every endpoint x {read,write,delete}; diff against intended matrix
techniques.oracle: a role reaches an endpoint it should not (200 vs expected 403)

techniques.how_to_test: spray common/leaked creds at login with lockout awareness; rate-limit test
techniques.oracle: successful auth; or no lockout (rate-limit finding)

techniques.how_to_test: test alg=none, key-confusion (RS->HS), weak secret crack, kid injection, expiry/replay
techniques.oracle: forged/altered token accepted by the server
techniques.real_world_basis: forged admin JWT via stolen signing key

techniques.how_to_test: state/PKCE, redirect_uri, token/company binding, session fixation, logout invalidation
techniques.oracle: CSRF/account-link works, or session survives logout

techniques.how_to_test: submit crafted serialized object with a benign side-effect marker to a deser sink (import/config/cookie)
techniques.oracle: marker fires (callback/file/DB) proving code path executed
techniques.real_world_basis: a package-registry Marshal deser -> RCE

techniques.how_to_test: dot-segment/encoded traversal (../ ..%2f ....//) on file-by-name/report/download endpoints; PHP wrappers
techniques.oracle: out-of-scope file content returned (e.g., /etc/passwd marker)
techniques.real_world_basis: a scientific data-file /proc/self/environ disclosure

techniques.how_to_test: upload crafted-but-valid files (webshell ext bypass, polyglot, malicious CSV/IIF/backup/dataset) that rewrite data or trigger parser side-effects
techniques.oracle: DB reflects planted content, or parser executes/discloses
techniques.real_world_basis: crafted dataset processed by worker returned secrets

techniques.how_to_test: set a user field to =/+/-/@ or DDE payload; export; inspect bytes
techniques.oracle: formula prefix survives unescaped into the exported file

techniques.how_to_test: negative/overflow/non-finite values across every money field + entity; copy-path bypass; unguarded state transitions
techniques.oracle: DB persists invalid money (negative/overflow) or a disallowed state

techniques.how_to_test: replay the same money-mutation POST N times (sequential + concurrent)
techniques.oracle: duplicate rows created (double-billing) with no 409/dedup

techniques.how_to_test: fire N concurrent requests at a check-then-write path (payment ceiling, allocation)
techniques.oracle: invariant violated under concurrency (over-payment, double-invoice)

techniques.how_to_test: fingerprint -> CVE RAG -> fire matching nuclei/msf/searchsploit exploit against the twin
techniques.oracle: exploit fires on the twin (refuted if not, unless twin diverges)

techniques.how_to_test: scan repos/pastes/breaches/web for owned-domain creds; validate + replay
techniques.oracle: cred authenticates; escalation battery confirms impact
techniques.real_world_basis: publicly-exposed third-party creds reused

techniques.desc: Data staging / pull-based C2 via shared store
techniques.how_to_test: check if a low-priv role can stage data into a store readable by an unauthorized party (public repo/bucket/export)
techniques.oracle: planted marker readable from the unauthorized side
techniques.real_world_basis: public dataset used as C2/exfil

techniques.how_to_test: enumerate SUID/caps/kernel/misconfig; kubelet/TokenRequest for k8s; run in the twin only
techniques.oracle: root/host or cluster-admin obtained in ground truth
techniques.real_world_basis: kernel CVE + kubelet -> host/cluster-admin

techniques.how_to_test: unthrottled mutation loops; unpaginated list growth; numeric-overflow 500s; slow endpoints
techniques.oracle: no rate-limit / unbounded response / hung request under volume

techniques.desc: AD/LDAP/Kerberos enumeration (users, SPNs, adminCount, delegation, trusts)
techniques.how_to_test: anonymous or credentialed bind to the DC; query servicePrincipalName / adminCount=1 / TRUSTED_FOR_DELEGATION; map to ATT&CK T1087.002/T1069.002
techniques.oracle: bind succeeds AND entries/SPNs returned
techniques.real_world_basis: kerberoasting + AD recon are the backbone of CS/BloodHound tradecraft

techniques.desc: Cloud/container discovery (AWS/Azure/GCP IAM, buckets, instances, managed identities)
techniques.how_to_test: with a credential, enumerate STS identity, IAM roles/policies, storage buckets, compute; T1526/T1580
techniques.oracle: cloud API returns caller identity + resource list
techniques.real_world_basis: cloud attack surface is where CS/MSF cloud modules focus

techniques.desc: Mass service/version/TLS fingerprinting feeding CVE correlation
techniques.how_to_test: -sV version scan + TLS cipher/JARM; feed banners to the RAG for CVE mapping; T1046
techniques.oracle: open service with a version banner
techniques.real_world_basis: Nmap/Masscan-grade enumeration is table stakes for MSF/CS recon

techniques.desc: External/passive attack-surface mapping (CT logs, passive DNS, subdomains)
techniques.how_to_test: OWNED domain only: pull %.<domain> from crt.sh, resolve, seed further probes; T1590/T1596
techniques.oracle: subdomains discovered from CT logs
techniques.real_world_basis: Shodan/Censys/CT-log surface mapping; owned-domain OSINT lane

techniques.desc: Credentialed file/config/secret discovery over SMB shares (read-only)
techniques.how_to_test: list shares, spider filenames, flag .env/.pem/.key/config/kdbx; NEVER download/write; T1039/T1552.001
techniques.oracle: readable share AND a secret-looking file present
techniques.real_world_basis: share spidering for secrets is core post-foothold recon

techniques.desc: Source-level supply-chain: lockfile deps vs known CVEs (complements image grype)
techniques.how_to_test: parse requirements.txt/package-lock.json/go.sum; query the offline RAG per dep; T1195.001
techniques.oracle: a lockfile dependency matches a known CVE
techniques.real_world_basis: transitive-dep CVEs are a top real-world entry vector

techniques.desc: NOVEL: cross-domain RAG inference of a hidden surface from uncorrelated signals
techniques.how_to_test: correlate TLS SANs + leaked keys + headers across gathered findings to infer an unprobed surface, then confirm by probing; T1592/T1595
techniques.oracle: the inferred hidden surface returns 2xx
techniques.real_world_basis: beyond every listed tool: none correlate across evidence domains

techniques.desc: NOVEL: grey-box fuzzing of auth/authz LOGIC (JWT alg=none, stripped sig, tampered claims)
techniques.how_to_test: mutate a captured JWT and replay to a protected path; a mutation ACCEPTED (2xx) is a bypass; T1211/T1078
techniques.oracle: a tampered token is accepted where a valid one is required
techniques.real_world_basis: fuzzing auth logic, not memory-safe parsers -- novel

techniques.desc: NOVEL: dependency-confusion / typosquat detection vs live registry
techniques.how_to_test: for each internal-looking dep, check if the name is CLAIMABLE (404) on PyPI/npm; T1195.002
techniques.oracle: an internal dependency name is unclaimed on the public registry
techniques.real_world_basis: dependency confusion is a live class no scanner in the set flags proactively

techniques.desc: NOVEL: deception-aware discovery via response timing/error baselining
techniques.how_to_test: probe distinct + random paths, baseline timing/length/code variance; near-zero variance = decoy; T1497
techniques.oracle: uniform length AND code across distinct paths with ~0 timing variance
techniques.real_world_basis: telling real surface from bait -- a modern red-team need none of the set automate

techniques.desc: NOVEL: graph attack-path analysis over confirmed discovery findings
techniques.how_to_test: build a reach graph from verified findings; BFS to the goal node; T1069/T1018
techniques.oracle: a confirmed path to the goal exists
techniques.real_world_basis: BloodHound-style pathing, driven by ORACLE-confirmed edges rather than raw ACLs

techniques.desc: Replay a state-mutating request N times; a non-idempotent handler with no total<=bound invariant over-applies the effect (e.g. duplicate/over-credit, double refund, double-settle).
techniques.how_to_test: setup a target record; MEASURE a business metric; REPLAY the mutation N>1x; measure again; oracle: idempotency (metric grows >1 unit) or invariant (sum<=bound violated after).
techniques.oracle: InvariantOracle (measured<=bound held before, violated after) OR IdempotencyOracle (delta>unit across N replays)
